When you ask the herald, the button that gives your shield a voice, Gemma , Google's open-weight model, writes a motto and a short piece of lore for those arms, and nothing else. What I Built In July I built 33 small web apps for Netlify's Hot AR Summer, with one rule: no Math.random anywhere. articles.title: UltraCanvas: a C++20 GUI framework for Windows, Linux, macOS and the browser
articles.excerpt: Every couple of years another C++ GUI framework turns up claiming one API for every desktop platform. Usually it turns out to be a thin wrapper over one native toolkit, and the other platforms are an…
articles.body: Every couple of years another C++ GUI framework turns up claiming one API for every desktop platform. Usually it turns out to be a thin wrapper over one native toolkit, and the other platforms are an afterthought. UltraCanvas is a newer one, and it looks further along than that. I spent the last few weeks running its builds on an ordinary Windows laptop and a Linux install, and this is what I found. The short version: a C++20 framework, CMake-based and MIT-licensed, with one API for windowing, rendering, input and events across Windows, Linux and macOS, plus a WebAssembly build you can open in a browser tab with nothing to install. Disclosure I work with the ULTRA OS team on developer outreach, and UltraCanvas is the graphics layer of that project.

articles.title: 'Reply With OK': Grok Build's CLI Still Uploaded the Whole Git History
articles.excerpt: Book: AI Agents Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who sh…
articles.body: Book: AI Agents Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub "Reply with exactly: OK. Do not read or open any files." That was the whole prompt. The researcher who publishes as cereblab sent it to Grok Build CLI 0.2.93, xAI's terminal coding agent, with mitmproxy sitting in the middle. The model answered. In the background, the CLI also posted a git bundle of the repository to xAI's storage endpoint: 4 commits, 47 files, full history. Cloning the captured bundle gave back a planted file the agent had been told not to open, marker string intact ( cereblab's write-up ).

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built after-flash PWA androidfirst Apparently, we are approaching the point where it is easier to slop together an app than to find the right one in the store. As someone who makes a living writing software, I’m not entirely sure I should be celebrating this. Anyway, I made a drawing app. It is called After Flash . One drawing tool. Three brush sizes. An eraser. Two layers: drawing and background color. No fill tool, no merging vectors. You can draw frame by frame, play the animation, and export individual drawings as SVG. There is also an AI color palette generator. Give it a theme, a mood, or a few words, and it suggests 8 or 64 colors you can use directly in your drawing. That’s roughly it.

articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.excerpt: The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.
articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: Vaonis unveils Atlas, the world's 1st modular smart telescope system
articles.excerpt: Pre-orders are now open for the Atlas, the new modular smart telescope from Vaonis which allows observation with two optical tubes.
articles.body: Vaonis has just announced its new generation of smart telescope technology, known as Atlas. Less of a single smart telescope and more of a new optical system, Atlas was designed with interchangeability and adaptability in mind. Its new SkyDock system allows two optical tubes to be connected and the telescope has live night sky monitoring to predict available observations. You can preorder the Vaonis Atlas with a single Atlas 80 module for $3,990, or $5,490 for the twin at Adorama . But it'll also soon be available at B&H and other retailers. Currently, there is only one optical tube, the Atlas 80, but Vaonis is planning to release add-on modules designed for looking at different night sky objects, including for planetary observation.
